playbook.rollback: Any endpoint loses reachability on the new leg -> fail back to the legacy leg (still up); re-validate.

device_dossiers.note: Risk index = topology impact (1-10) x stacked exposure (0-10) per asset, mirroring asset-risk practice (likelihood x impact). Synthesis of already-computed axes only; an axis without evidence is 'not assessed', never red.

checks.title: Distribution/core tier present
checks.observed: 4 L3 node(s) (gateway SVI or routing adjacency) front 19 L2 access node(s).
checks.implication: A defined L3 tier bounds failure domains and gives the migration a stable anchor.
checks.recommendation: Carry the tiering into the target design; keep gateway functions at the distribution tier.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — hierarchical access/distribution/core model

checks.title: No daisy-chained access switches
checks.observed: Every observed access uplink lands on the L3 tier.
checks.implication: Failure domains stay bounded per closet.
checks.recommendation: Preserve the star topology in the target design.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — each access switch homes to the distribution layer

checks.title: Dual-homed access uplinks
checks.observed: 17 of 19 access switch(es) reach exactly ONE in-fleet neighbour: access1, access10, access11, access12, access13, access14, access15, access16, access17, access2, access3, access4 +5 more.
checks.implication: A single uplink (or single upstream switch) is a per-closet single point of failure — one optic, one linecard or one upstream chassis takes the closet down.
checks.recommendation: Dual-home each listed switch to two distribution nodes (or at minimum two linecards) as part of the migration build.
checks.reference: Cisco campus HA design — redundant uplinks from every access switch

checks.title: First-hop redundancy on every gateway
checks.observed: VLAN(s) 30 are served by a SINGLE gateway with no FHRP peer.
checks.implication: Losing that one gateway device black-holes every endpoint on the VLAN — the highest-impact availability exposure a campus carries, and a migration-readiness FAIL.
checks.recommendation: Add an FHRP peer (or move the VLAN behind a redundant gateway pair) BEFORE any migration wave touches these VLANs.
checks.reference: Cisco campus HA design — FHRP (HSRP/VRRP/GLBP) on every shared gateway

checks.title: Redundant power supplies
checks.observed: Power-supply inventory was not captured for any device.
checks.recommendation: Include 'show environment power' / inventory output in collection.
checks.reference: Cisco campus HA design — N+1 power on aggregation nodes

checks.title: No keystone single point of failure
checks.observed: Losing core1 strands 45 endpoint(s); access1 strands 42 endpoint(s); core2 strands 42 endpoint(s); access13 strands 39 endpoint(s); access14 strands 39 endpoint(s).
checks.implication: Endpoint dependency is concentrated — these devices ARE the availability budget.
checks.recommendation: Verify each keystone's redundancy (uplinks, power, supervisor) and sequence them with the most conservative cutover plan (their waves carry the widest blast radius).
checks.reference: Availability analysis — single-device blast radius

checks.title: Deterministic STP root at the distribution tier
checks.observed: Access switch(es) hold the STP root: access1 roots 1 VLAN(s); access10 roots 1 VLAN(s); access11 roots 1 VLAN(s); access12 roots 1 VLAN(s); access13 roots 1 VLAN(s); access14 roots 1 VLAN(s).
checks.implication: A root on an access closet means the L2 tree converges around the smallest box in the fabric — default (un-pinned) priorities usually caused it, and any new switch can silently steal the root.
checks.recommendation: Pin root primary/secondary priorities on the distribution pair for every VLAN.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — pin the STP root (priority) at the distribution layer

checks.title: Edge protection (BPDU Guard) on access ports
checks.observed: BPDU Guard state was not captured for the access ports.
checks.recommendation: Include 'show spanning-tree interface detail' (or run-config) in collection.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — PortFast + BPDU Guard on every edge port

checks.title: VLAN 1 not used for user traffic
checks.observed: Trunks with native VLAN 1 on 17 switch(es): access1, access10, access11, access12, access2, access3, access4, access5, access6, access7, access8, access9 +5 more.
checks.implication: Native VLAN 1 on inter-switch trunks exposes untagged control-plane crosstalk and is flagged by the hardening baseline.
checks.recommendation: Set the native VLAN to a dedicated unused VLAN on the listed trunks.
checks.reference: Cisco hardening guidance — keep user traffic and trunk native VLAN off VLAN 1

checks.title: Bounded broadcast domains
checks.observed: Largest observed VLAN carries 3 endpoint(s) — within the conventional envelope.
checks.implication: Broadcast domains are bounded.
checks.recommendation: Keep VLAN sizing within a /24-/23 of endpoints in the target design.
checks.reference: Campus design guidance — constrain broadcast domains (≈ a /23 of endpoints per VLAN)

checks.title: Trunks pruned to required VLANs
checks.observed: All 28 trunk(s) with captured lists are pruned.
checks.implication: VLAN scope stays bounded per closet.
checks.recommendation: Maintain pruning in the per-wave port maps.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — prune trunk allowed-VLAN lists to the required set

checks.title: Every access VLAN has a gateway in scope
checks.observed: All 5 access VLAN(s) terminate on an in-scope gateway SVI.
checks.implication: The L2/L3 boundary is fully accounted for.
checks.recommendation: Keep the gateway register in the LLD as the addressing source of truth.
checks.reference: Campus L3 design — every user VLAN terminates on a known, redundant gateway

checks.title: DHCP relay on endpoint-serving gateways
checks.observed: 3 endpoint-carrying VLAN(s) have a gateway with no DHCP relay configured: VLAN(s) 30, 40, 41.
checks.implication: If those clients use central DHCP, the missing helper is a silent post-cutover black hole (the classic day-1 failure); if addressing is static/local this is by design.
checks.recommendation: Confirm the addressing model per VLAN; add helpers where central DHCP is intended before the carrying wave.
checks.reference: Campus L3 design — ip helper-address on every client-serving SVI

checks.title: Single IGP, controlled redistribution
checks.observed: 3 redistribution edge(s) observed.
checks.implication: Every extra protocol and redistribution point is a loop/suboptimal-routing risk and a troubleshooting tax; migrations are when undocumented redistribution bites.
checks.recommendation: Plan convergence to a single IGP in the target design; until then, document each redistribution edge (route-map, direction, owner) in the LLD.
checks.reference: Campus L3 design — one IGP where possible; document every redistribution boundary

checks.title: FHRP active aligned with the STP root
checks.observed: No VLAN has both a known FHRP active gateway and an observed root bridge.
checks.recommendation: Collect 'show standby'/'show spanning-tree' together to enable this check.
checks.reference: Cisco campus design — co-locate the FHRP active gateway with the STP root per VLAN

checks.title: Access uplink oversubscription within 20:1
checks.observed: 19 access switch(es) measured; worst provisioned ratio 1:1.
checks.implication: Uplink capacity is within the conventional envelope.
checks.recommendation: Re-validate ratios whenever the target design changes uplink counts or speeds.
checks.reference: Cisco campus rule of thumb — ≤20:1 access→distribution, ≤4:1 distribution→core

checks.title: Port-capacity headroom for growth
checks.observed: access1 at 100.0% port utilisation; access10 at 100.0% port utilisation; access11 at 100.0% port utilisation; access12 at 100.0% port utilisation; access2 at 100.0% port utilisation; access3 at 100.0% port utilisation.
checks.implication: A full closet forces ad-hoc daisy-chaining (see HIER-2) the day a port is needed.
checks.recommendation: Size replacement hardware with ≥10% spare ports per listed closet.
checks.reference: Capacity planning — keep ~10% port headroom per closet

checks.title: No operational drift / false health
checks.observed: 1 lower-severity drift finding(s).
checks.implication: Low-grade drift compounds; the migration touch is the cheapest moment to clear it.
checks.recommendation: Fold the items into the per-wave work orders.
checks.reference: Assessment doctrine — configured is not healthy; up is not healthy

checks.title: Clean configuration hygiene
checks.observed: 2 undefined reference(s) across 1 device(s): core1.
checks.implication: A referenced-but-undefined ACL/route-map fails OPEN or CLOSED depending on platform — either way it is latent surprise during cutover.
checks.recommendation: Resolve or remove each undefined reference before its device migrates.
checks.reference: Operational hygiene — no undefined references in running configuration

checks.title: Collection confidence
checks.observed: Collection is complete across the fleet.
checks.implication: The review stands on full evidence.
checks.reference: Assessment doctrine — state collection blind spots explicitly

checks.title: Management-plane hardening (CIS baseline)
checks.observed: 1 device(s) grade WEAK (a high-severity hardening check fails): core1.
checks.implication: A weak management plane (open HTTP/Smart Install, missing AAA, default communities) is the attack surface that turns a migration window into an incident.
checks.recommendation: Apply the generated remediation snippets to the WEAK devices first — before any maintenance window publicises change activity.
checks.reference: CIS Cisco IOS Benchmark — AAA, NTP, logging, SSHv2/VTY, SNMPv3 hardening

checks.title: Segmentation enforced at the L3 boundary
checks.observed: 1 VRF(s) in use; 2 of 9 gateway SVIs carry an ACL.
checks.implication: Partial enforcement leaves unpoliced inter-segment paths.
checks.recommendation: Close the unpoliced SVIs (or fold them into a VRF) in the target design.
checks.reference: Segmentation guidance — enforce inter-segment policy at the L3 boundary (VRF / gateway ACL)

checks.title: No hardware past end-of-support
checks.observed: 5 device(s) are past LAST-DAY-OF-SUPPORT (and 6 past end-of-sale): access1, access10, access12, access13, access15, access16, access3, access4, access6, access7, access9.
checks.implication: Past LDoS there is NO TAC escalation path and no software fix — a fault during a migration window on these devices has no vendor backstop.
checks.recommendation: Replace (not upgrade) the LDoS devices as the first migration waves; stage spares for any that must briefly remain.
checks.reference: Cisco EoX policy — no TAC/software support past last-day-of-support

checks.title: One software image per platform
checks.observed: Every platform runs a single image.
checks.implication: Troubleshooting and rollback are uniform per model.
checks.recommendation: Pin the images as the minimum-version baseline in the LLD.
checks.reference: AS LLD convention — minimise image variance per platform
